papers.title: ReMoD-Mol: Reliability-Aware Multimodal Learning with Descriptor-Guided Knowledge Distillation for Molecular Property Prediction
papers.summary: Abstract Motivation Accurate molecular property prediction (MPP) remains a central challenge in drug discovery. Given the limited availability of labeled molecular data, multimodal molecular representation learning offers a promising means of integrating complementary structural information for MPP. Existing multimodal models still face two limitations: (i) common fusion strategies, particularly direct concatenation, can introduce redundant information or signals that are weakly relevant to the target property; and (ii) the effective incorporation of complementary physicochemical priors into multimodal representations remains insufficiently explored. Results Here, we proposed ReMoD-Mol, a reliability-aware multimodal framework that integrated molecular graphs, SMILES sequences and two-dimensional molecular images. Task-adaptive modality calibration learned one set of weights per benchmark from downstream supervision to regulate the relative contributions of the three molecular views. Descriptor- and fingerprint-based teachers further provided task-conditioned chemical priors through train-only, five-fold out-of-fold knowledge distillation. Prototype-guided embedding shaping together with graph-view and SMILES-view consistency objectives regularized the fused representation space. Across nine MoleculeNet benchmark datasets spanning regression and classification, ReMoD-Mol achieved the best mean performance on seven datasets and the second-best on the other two in a scaffold-split comparison with 14 baselines. Representation analyses revealed smoother property-related manifolds and more discriminative class structures, while learned modality coefficients exhibited distinct task-dependent fusion patterns. Teacher-prior and ablation analyses further supported the complementary roles of chemical-prior transfer and multi-view representation regularization. Availability and implementation Source code, processed datasets and implementation details are publicly available at https://github.com/27167199/ReMoD-Mol

papers.title: Data-Driven Modeling of Promoter Affection to 5’ Untranslated Region Design for Rational Predictive Translational Engineering
papers.summary: Abstract Motivation Precise gene expression control is fundamental for biological research and synthetic systems. While biophysical models predict transcriptional or translational regulation, they often overlook their potential interplay. Combining these regulations offers synergistic control, but its influence remains incompletely understood. Results Here, we investigated how promoter replacement affects 5’ untranslated region (5’ UTR)-mediated translation while designing the sequence of Escherichia coli . Using predictive models and a comprehensive library of promoter-5’ UTR pairs, we characterized the interference of promoters with translation rates in terms of mRNA secondary structures, especially the alternative folding of the Shine-Dalgarno (SD) region and frequency of the major transcription start sites (TSSs), which leads to the misprediction of gene expression. Availability Based on this, we developed UTR Designer Pro, a model for designing promoter-5’ UTR sequences with higher accuracy, now available as a web service at https://sbi.postech.ac.kr/utr_designer_pro/ . Our work improves understanding of transcriptional and translational regulation, aiding gene expression control in bacterial systems

all_papers.title: ReMoD-Mol: Reliability-Aware Multimodal Learning with Descriptor-Guided Knowledge Distillation for Molecular Property Prediction
all_papers.summary: Abstract Motivation Accurate molecular property prediction (MPP) remains a central challenge in drug discovery. Given the limited availability of labeled molecular data, multimodal molecular representation learning offers a promising means of integrating complementary structural information for MPP. Existing multimodal models still face two limitations: (i) common fusion strategies, particularly direct concatenation, can introduce redundant information or signals that are weakly relevant to the target property; and (ii) the effective incorporation of complementary physicochemical priors into multimodal representations remains insufficiently explored. Results Here, we proposed ReMoD-Mol, a reliability-aware multimodal framework that integrated molecular graphs, SMILES sequences and two-dimensional molecular images. Task-adaptive modality calibration learned one set of weights per benchmark from downstream supervision to regulate the relative contributions of the three molecular views. Descriptor- and fingerprint-based teachers further provided task-conditioned chemical priors through train-only, five-fold out-of-fold knowledge distillation. Prototype-guided embedding shaping together with graph-view and SMILES-view consistency objectives regularized the fused representation space. Across nine MoleculeNet benchmark datasets spanning regression and classification, ReMoD-Mol achieved the best mean performance on seven datasets and the second-best on the other two in a scaffold-split comparison with 14 baselines. Representation analyses revealed smoother property-related manifolds and more discriminative class structures, while learned modality coefficients exhibited distinct task-dependent fusion patterns. Teacher-prior and ablation analyses further supported the complementary roles of chemical-prior transfer and multi-view representation regularization. Availability and implementation Source code, processed datasets and implementation details are publicly available at https://github.com/27167199/ReMoD-Mol

all_papers.title: Data-Driven Modeling of Promoter Affection to 5’ Untranslated Region Design for Rational Predictive Translational Engineering
all_papers.summary: Abstract Motivation Precise gene expression control is fundamental for biological research and synthetic systems. While biophysical models predict transcriptional or translational regulation, they often overlook their potential interplay. Combining these regulations offers synergistic control, but its influence remains incompletely understood. Results Here, we investigated how promoter replacement affects 5’ untranslated region (5’ UTR)-mediated translation while designing the sequence of Escherichia coli . Using predictive models and a comprehensive library of promoter-5’ UTR pairs, we characterized the interference of promoters with translation rates in terms of mRNA secondary structures, especially the alternative folding of the Shine-Dalgarno (SD) region and frequency of the major transcription start sites (TSSs), which leads to the misprediction of gene expression. Availability Based on this, we developed UTR Designer Pro, a model for designing promoter-5’ UTR sequences with higher accuracy, now available as a web service at https://sbi.postech.ac.kr/utr_designer_pro/ . Our work improves understanding of transcriptional and translational regulation, aiding gene expression control in bacterial systems

Using predictive models and a comprehensive library of promoter-5' UTR pairs, we characterized the interference of promoters with translation rates in terms of mRNA secondary structures, especially the alternative folding of the Shine-Dalgarno (SD) region and frequency of the major transcription start sites (TSSs), which leads to the misprediction of gene expression.

AVAILABILITY: Based on this, we developed UTR Designer Pro, a model for designing promoter-5' UTR sequences with higher accuracy, now available as a web service at https://sbi.postech.ac.kr/utr_designer_pro/. Our work improves understanding of transcriptional and translational regulation, aiding gene expression control in bacterial systems.

Combining these regulations offers synergistic control, but its influence remains incompletely understood.

RESULTS: Here, we investigated how promoter replacement affects 5' untranslated region (5' UTR)-mediated translation while designing the sequence of Escherichia coli. Using predictive models and a comprehensive library of promoter-5' UTR pairs, we characterized the interference of promoters with translation rates in terms of mRNA secondary structures, especially the alternative folding of the Shine-Dalgarno (SD) region and frequency of the major transcription start sites (TSSs), which leads to the misprediction of gene expression.

AVAILABILITY: Based on this, we developed UTR Designer Pro, a model for designing promoter-5' UTR sequences with higher accuracy, now available as a web service at https://sbi.postech.ac.kr/utr_designer_pro/. Our work improves understanding of transcriptional and translational regulation, aiding gene expression control in bacterial systems.

SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION: Supplementary data are available at Bioinformatics online.
